text: From SR 20 at Mazama follow Lost River Road to the end of the pavement, then the narrow gravel Harts Pass Road (FR 5400) to Harts Pass. At the guard station cabin turn right onto Slate Peak Road (FR 5400-600) and climb to the Slate Pass Trailhead at the second switchback beyond the horse loading area, about 6,900 ft. The road is usually open July to September. Fill out the free self-issue Pasayten

From Sedro-Woolley, drive SR 20 east about 16 miles to milepost 82 and turn north on Baker Lake Road (FS 11). Continue about 18 miles; just past Boulder Creek Campground and the Boulder Creek bridge, turn left on FS 1130 for about 1 mile, then left on FS 1131 to the road end and the Boulder Ridge Trailhead (Trail #605) at about 2,700 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

From Sedro-Woolley, drive SR 20 east 16 miles to milepost 82 and turn left (north) on Baker Lake Road (FS 11). Continue about 18 miles; just past Boulder Creek Campground and the Boulder Creek bridge, turn left on FR-1130 for about 1 mile, then left on FR-1131 to its end at the Boulder Ridge Trailhead, around 2,700 ft. Boulder Ridge Trail #605 starts from the road's end. This is the lowest trailhe

Drive the Harts Pass Road (FR 5400) up from Mazama and turn right at Harts Pass onto FR 5400-600 toward Slate Peak for about 3.5 miles to the Slate Pass trailhead at a switchback. It is one of the highest drivable roads in the state and typically does not clear of snow until early to mid summer, so check its status before committing.

FR-5130 (Eightmile Creek Road) climbs out of the Methow valley to the signed pullout at about 3,810 ft, with room for only five to seven cars. No fee or permit is needed to park. The road holds snow well into spring, so check its condition before committing to the drive.

From Winthrop, drive north about 8 miles on West Chewuch Road (County Road 1213) to Eightmile Road (Forest Road 5130). Follow Eightmile Road roughly 12 to 15 miles northwest along Eightmile Creek to the Copper Glance Trailhead, at about 3,800 feet. There is no fee here.

Drive Baker Lake Road (Forest Road 11) north from WA-20 at milepost 82, near Concrete, about 25.5 miles to its end at the Baker River Trailhead, about 774 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or day-use fee is required.

From Sedro-Woolley, follow SR 20 east 16 miles to milepost 82, turn north on Baker Lake Road (FR 11) for 14 miles to Baker Dam Road, cross the Upper Baker Dam, continue 8 miles on FR 1107, then turn onto spur FR 1107022 and follow it to the road-end trailhead. Pavement ends at Baker Dam Road; everything beyond it is gravel Forest Service road.

text: From I-5 Exit 255 in Bellingham, take SR 542 (Mount Baker Highway) east about 16.7 miles and turn right on Mosquito Lake Road. After about 4.8 miles, just south of Porter Creek, turn left onto Middle Fork Road (Road 38) and follow it about 4.8 miles, then turn right down to the gated bridge over the Middle Fork Nooksack and park at the gate, about 1,200 ft. Beyond is private timberland; a landowne

Drive Baker Lake Road (Forest Road 11) north from SR 20 near milepost 82, then turn onto FR 1152 and follow the 1152-014 spur to its end at about 2,500 feet, where the trail begins. The spur is rough and rutted, so high clearance is the sensible minimum for the drive in. If you're staying overnight in the park, you'll need a North Cascades backcountry permit, obtained in person at Marblemount or a

From SR 20 at milepost 82 near Concrete, turn north on Baker Lake Road (FS Road 11) and drive about 24 miles to FS Road 1152, directly across from Shannon Creek Campground. Turn left on 1152, then take a sharp right onto spur 1152-014 and follow it to the road end at about 2,500 ft. The gravel can be potholed but is passable to most cars. A Northwest Forest Pass or equivalent recreation pass is re

pins.name: Andrews Creek Trailhead (Trail #504, end of pavement on FS 51)

text: From Highway 20 in Winthrop, turn onto County Road 1213 (West Chewuch Road) and follow it about 6 miles to where it joins Forest Road 51. Continue north on FR 51 to the end of the pavement and turn right into the Andrews Creek Trailhead at 3,050 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass is needed to park, and a free self-issued Pasayten Wilderness permit is required.

Drive West Chewuch Road / FR-51 north out of Winthrop roughly 22-23 miles to the road end at about 3,050 ft. Everything above is gained on foot — this is one of the longest wilderness approaches in the state, and the Chewuch River trailhead to the east is a longer alternative to the same camp.

From Highway 20 in Winthrop, turn onto County Road 1213 (West Chewuch Road) and follow it about 6 miles to where it joins Forest Road 51. Continue north on FR 51 to the end of the pavement and turn right into the Andrews Creek Trailhead at 3,050 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass is needed to park, and a free self-issued Pasayten Wilderness permit is required.

The trailhead sits at roughly 3,400 to 3,700 ft on Glacier Creek Road 39. The road washed out in December 2025 and reopened to vehicles in August 2026 after repairs; it has washed out before, so check its status before committing.

From the Mount Baker Highway (SR 542), drive about 1 mile east of the Glacier Public Service Center and turn right onto Glacier Creek Road (FS Road 39). Follow it about 8 miles to the Heliotrope Ridge Trailhead at roughly 3,700 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or the daily fee is required to park, and a free Mount Baker Wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead.

The trailhead is at the end of Glacier Creek Road (Forest Road 39), about eight miles off Highway 542, at roughly 3,700 feet. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and you self-issue a Mount Baker Wilderness permit at the kiosk there. Check current road status before you drive up, since conditions on FR-39 can vary.
From the Mount Baker Highway (SR 542) about a mile east of Glacier, turn onto Glacier Creek Road (FR 39) and follow it to its end at the Heliotrope Ridge trailhead for Trail 677, at about 3,700 ft.

From SR 20 in Winthrop, take East Chewuch Road north about 7 miles and turn right onto FR 51. Continue north up the Chewuch valley, staying on the road as it becomes FR 5160, to its end at the Thirtymile Trailhead, about 3,400 ft, where the Chewuch River Trail #510 begins. A free self-issued Pasayten Wilderness permit is required.

Park at the Thirtymile Trailhead, at the end of West Chewuch Road, about 29 miles north of Winthrop. A Northwest Forest Pass and a free self-issue Pasayten Wilderness permit, available at the trailhead kiosk, are both required, and there is no potable water on site. The road in and the high country beyond often don't fully clear of snow until late June or early July, so plan an early-season trip a

pins.name: Artist Point Trailhead (Chain Lakes/Ptarmigan Ridge Trail)

text: From I-5 Exit 255 in Bellingham, follow the Mount Baker Highway (WA-542) east through Glacier and past the Heather Meadows ski area to the road end at Artist Point, about 58 miles. The final stretch is usually snow-free only from about mid-July into early fall. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

From I-5 Exit 255 in Bellingham, follow SR 542, the Mount Baker Highway, east through Glacier and past the Mt. Baker Ski Area and Heather Meadows to the road's end at the Artist Point parking lot, about 5,100 ft. The last stretch opens only once the snow is cleared, usually in summer. A Northwest Forest Pass or day-use fee is required to park.
The trailhead is on the east side of the Mount Baker Highway (SR-542), about a mile below Artist Point, at roughly 4,770 feet.

Drive Mount Baker Highway (SR 542) to its end at the Austin Pass/Artist Point trailhead, a paved lot roughly 58 miles and 1.5-2 hours from Bellingham. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and overnight parties sign the wilderness register at the trailhead; no camping permit is needed. The upper highway to Austin Pass typically doesn't open until late June or early July, depending on snowpa

pins.name: Windy Peak Trailhead / Long Swamp Campground

text: From Tonasket, cross the Okanogan River and drive west on Loomis-Oroville Road to Loomis. Just north of town turn onto Toats Coulee Road, County Road 9425, which becomes 4066 and then FR-39, and follow it roughly 20 miles to the junction with FR-3900-300 at Long Swamp Campground, about 5,500 ft. That last stretch is a long dirt road and is often not reliably clear of snow and debris until late Jun

pins.name: White Salmon Road (hairpin) TH / lower White Salmon lodge

text: Drive the Mount Baker Highway (SR-542) to the town of Glacier and stop at the Glacier Public Service Center for the backcountry permit — it's required, not optional. Continue up SR-542 to around mile 51-52 and take the hairpin turn onto NF-3075 (White Salmon Road), just before the White Salmon Day Lodge, to the small pull-off at the old White Salmon Lodge site.

pins.name: White Salmon Lodge road gate (Mount Baker Highway hairpin)

text: From Glacier, drive the Mount Baker Highway (SR-542) east about 18 miles to the hairpin switchback at roughly 3,500 ft, below the ski area, and park in the small pull-off at the gated White Salmon Road (FS 3075). Parking is very limited and is not allowed on the highway shoulder; do not block the gate. No parking pass is required.

From I-5 Exit 255 in Bellingham, follow SR 542, the Mount Baker Highway, east about 56 miles through Glacier to the Heather Meadows area at the Mt. Baker Ski Area. Turn into the large parking lot signed for Bagley Lakes, at about 4,200 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass is required to park.

From Glacier, drive SR-542 east about 7.5 miles to the Wells Creek / Nooksack Falls junction near milepost 41 and turn right onto gravel FS Road 33. Stay on the main road roughly 11 to 12 miles to its end at an unsigned parking area in an old clearcut at about 4,900 ft. The last miles are rocky and cross-ditched, so high clearance helps, and the road is gated seasonally from November into early Ju

From Glacier, drive SR-542 east about 1 mile past the Glacier Public Service Center, turn right onto Glacier Creek Road (FS Road 39), then immediately left onto Deadhorse Road (FS Road 37). Follow FS 37 about 13 miles to the trailhead lot at its end. FS 37 has been closed by a flood washout near milepost 3 since 2021, so check its status before planning to drive to the trailhead. A Northwest Fores

The Nooksack Cirque trailhead for Trail #750 sits at the end of Nooksack Cirque Road (FS-34), about a mile up from Hannegan Pass Road (FS-32) off the Mount Baker Highway, at about 2,200 ft. Cars stop on the near side of Ruth Creek: there is no bridge at the trailhead, and the crossing is made on foot on a large logjam a little downstream, with the trail and its registry box picked up on the far ba

From Glacier, drive Mt. Baker Highway (SR-542) east about 12.5 miles, then turn left onto Hannegan Pass Road (FR-32). Continue just over a mile to the junction with Nooksack Cirque Road (FR-34) and follow FR-34 one mile to its end at the Nooksack Cirque Trailhead, which is a different trailhead from the Hannegan Pass Trailhead further up FR-32. Ford Ruth Creek right at the trailhead — there's no b

Reach the trailhead via Hannegan Pass Road (FS-32), off SR 542 near Glacier, about two miles up from the Glacier Public Service Center. Day-use parking is on both sides of the road, with a vault toilet on site, and a Northwest Forest Pass is required.

From Loomis, drive north on County Road 9425 for 2 miles, then turn left onto Toats Coulee Road (County Road 4066), which becomes FR 39. Follow it about 14 miles to the spur signed for Iron Gate, FR 3900-500, and drive that about 6 miles to the trailhead. FR 3900-500 is a rough high-clearance road, not for passenger cars or trailers. A Northwest Forest Pass or day fee is required to park, plus a f

pins.name: Hannegan Trailhead (Hannegan Pass Trail #674 road end)

text: Drive the Mount Baker Highway to Hannegan Pass Road (FS-32) and follow it to the road end at about 3,100 ft, where Hannegan Pass Trail #674 starts. A Northwest Forest Pass is required at the kiosk here.

The route begins at Hannegan Campground, a road-end trailhead at the very end of Ruth Creek Road (Forest Road 32), at about 3,100 feet. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park here, and a self-issue wilderness permit is needed once you continue on into North Cascades National Park.

From Glacier, drive the Mount Baker Highway (SR-542) east about 12.5 miles and turn left onto Hannegan Pass Road (FS Road 32). Follow it 5.3 miles to the road-end parking at the Hannegan Trailhead. A recreation pass such as the Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a North Cascades National Park backcountry permit is required for camps inside the park.

pins.name: Tomyhoi Lake / Yellow Aster Butte Trailhead

text: From Glacier, follow SR 542 (Mount Baker Highway) east about 12 miles and turn left onto Twin Lakes Road (FR 3065) at the east end of the WSDOT Shuksan maintenance facility. Drive 4.5 miles up the switchbacks to the Tomyhoi Lake / Yellow Aster Butte Trailhead, where roadside parking is limited. A Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass is required.

From Glacier, drive east on SR 542 (Mt. Baker Highway) about 12 miles to the WSDOT Shuksan maintenance facility and turn onto Twin Lakes Road (FS-3065). The first 4.5 miles are passenger-car friendly, reaching the Yellow Aster Butte/Tomyhoi Lake trailhead; beyond that the road narrows, turns rocky, and is not maintained for passenger vehicles, so high-clearance is recommended and 4WD helps for the

Drive Twin Lakes Road to its end at about 5,200 ft. The final miles are rough and deeply rutted, and many parties park short and walk them rather than risk the car. A Northwest Forest Pass is required; the signed High Pass Trail starts from the parking area.
